title: Search by One-One Restriction Queries
statement: Let an encoded maximization problem consist of a language of valid Boolean-string instances, a feasibility relation between instances and Boolean-string solutions, a rational objective value for each instance-solution pair, and a rational optimum for each instance; assume every feasible solution on a valid instance has value at most that optimum. A one-one restriction search for this problem is a polynomial-time map from decision procedures to reconstruction procedures such that, for every decision procedure and valid instance, the reconstructed solution is feasible, and every valid instance has optimum at most $1$. Moreover, whenever the decision procedure distinguishes the problem’s exact-one promise, every valid instance whose optimum is $1$ has a reconstructed solution of value exactly $1$.
hypotheses_covered: The problem has a language of valid Boolean-string instances
The problem has a feasibility relation on instance-solution pairs
The problem has a rational objective value on instance-solution pairs
The problem has a rational optimum for each instance
Every feasible solution on a valid instance has value at most the optimum
Reconstruction is a polynomial-time map from decision procedures to reconstruction procedures
Reconstruction is feasible for every decision procedure and every valid instance
The optimum is at most $1$ on every valid instance
A decision procedure distinguishing the exact-one promise yields value $1$ on every valid instance with optimum $1$
